_meta.indication: ZEVTERA is indicated for adults with Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection (bacteremia) including right-sided infective endocarditis; adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI); and adult and pediatric patients (3 months to <18 years) with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP), each caused by susceptible isolates.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, multicenter noninferiority trial versus daptomycin +/- aztreonam; prespecified noninferiority margin 15%.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection (bacteremia), including right-sided infective endocarditis, caused by methicillin-susceptible and methicillin-resistant isolates.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall success at the post-treatment evaluation (PTE) visit at Day 70 after randomization in the mITT population, assessed by the independent Data Review Committee.
pivotal_trials.n: 387 patients in the mITT population (189 ZEVTERA, 198 daptomycin +/- aztreonam)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall success 69.8% (132/189) ZEVTERA vs 68.7% (136/198) comparator; between-group difference 2.0% (95% CI -7.1, 11.1), meeting the noninferiority threshold.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, multicenter noninferiority trial versus vancomycin plus aztreonam; prespecified noninferiority margin of 10%.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (cellulitis/erysipelas, major cutaneous abscess, wound infection) with a lesion area of at least 75 cm2.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Early clinical response 48-72 hours after start of treatment, assessed in the ITT population.
pivotal_trials.n: 679 patients randomized (335 ZEVTERA, 344 vancomycin plus aztreonam)
pivotal_trials.result: Early clinical response 91.3% (306/335) ZEVTERA vs 88.1% (303/344) comparator; between-group difference 3.3% (95% CI -1.2, 7.8), meeting noninferiority.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trial 3 (BAP248/307-type CABP trial), the adult CABP pivotal trial
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, multicenter noninferiority study versus ceftriaxone with optional linezolid.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults hospitalized with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia requiring IV antibacterial treatment.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical cure rates at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit, 7 to 14 days after end-of-treatment, in the co-primary ITT and CE populations.
pivotal_trials.n: 638 patients in the ITT population (314 ZEVTERA, 324 ceftriaxone +/- linezolid)
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical cure at TOC (ITT) 76.4% (240/314) ZEVTERA vs 79.3% (257/324) comparator; difference -2.9% (95% CI -9.3, 3.6), meeting noninferiority.

key_safety: In SAB (Trial 1) the most common adverse reactions (>=4%) were anemia (12%), nausea (10%), hypokalemia (9%), vomiting (8%), hepatic enzyme and bilirubin increased (8%), and diarrhea (7%); serious adverse reactions occurred in 18.8% of ZEVTERA-treated SAB patients. In ABSSSI (Trial 2), most common (>=2%) were nausea (11%), diarrhea (6%), and headache (6%). In CABP (Trial 3), most common were nausea (10%), hepatic enzyme increased (10%), and vomiting (9%). Serious warnings include hypersensitivity reactions and seizures/CNS reactions.
target_moa: Ceftobiprole is a cephalosporin antibacterial that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to multiple penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) and inhibiting their transpeptidase activity, including high affinity for PBP2a in methicillin-resistant S. aureus.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not presented at an advisory committee meeting; no review issues required Advisory Committee advice.

basis.text: Ceftobiprole medocaril was granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation for CABP (July 20, 2015), ABSSSI (August 7, 2015), and SAB (December 8, 2017).

citations.quote: Ceftobiprole medocaril for injection was granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product designation for the CABP, acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI), and *Staphylococcus aureus* bacteremia (SAB) indications on July 20, 2015, August 7, 2015, and December 8, 2017, respectively.

summary.text: ZEVTERA (NDA 218275) received a traditional approval (not accelerated) based on three phase 3 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled noninferiority trials that met their prespecified endpoints. The product had Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation under the GAIN Act for its CABP, ABSSSI, and SAB indications, and the application received priority review designation. A five-year US surveillance study for ceftobiprole resistance is a required postmarketing commitment.

citations.quote: All three indications were supported by phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active controlled noninferiority (NI) trials which met their respective primary endpoints within the prespecified NI margins.

Ceftobiprole medocaril for injection was granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product designation for the CABP, acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI), and *Staphylococcus aureus* bacteremia (SAB) indications on July 20, 2015, August 7, 2015, and December 8, 2017, respectively.
The NDA received priority review designation on September 28, 2023, and was filed on October 02, 2023.
